identity.title: HerMES: ALMA Imaging of Herschel-selected Dusty Star-forming Galaxies

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present 870$\,\mu$m 0$\ensuremath{''}$45 resolution imaging from the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) of 29 HerMES DSFGs

targets.name: 29 HerMES Herschel-selected DSFGs (e.g. HXMM01, HXMM02, HADFS01, HECDFS12)

question.value: How does gravitational lensing and multiplicity affect the properties of the brightest Herschel-selected DSFGs, and what do the lens models imply for the bright end of the intrinsic DSFG number counts?

evidence.quote: Three aspects of our dataset make it uniquely suited to improving our understanding of the bright end of the intrinsic DSFG number counts.

method.value: uvmcmcfit: elliptical Gaussian sources, SIE lenses, ray tracing, compare model visibilities to data

evidence.quote: Sources are assumed to be elliptical Gaussians that are parameterized by the following six free parameters
We employ a “burn-in” phase with 512 walkers and 500-1000 iterations

key_parameters.value: uniform priors; theta_E 0.1-6 arcsec; q_lens>0.3; q_s>0.2; r_s 0.01-1.5 arcsec

evidence.quote: The axial ratios of the lenses and sources are restricted to be $q_{\rm lens} > 0.3$ and $q_{\rm s} > 0.2$.

assumptions.value: Additional lenses at same redshift as primary; maximal-lensing Einstein radii fixed for weakly lensed systems

evidence.quote: We assume secondary, tertiary, etc., lenses are located at the same redshift as the primary lens.

fitting.value: emcee affine-invariant ensemble MCMC with Gaussian likelihood in visibility plane

evidence.quote: We use emcee (cite: Foreman-Mackey:2013yq) to sample the posterior probability density function (PDF) of our model parameters.

results_numeric.quantity: Number of ALMA sources above 5 sigma

evidence.quote: We identify 62 sources down to the $5\sigma$ point-source sensitivity limit in our ALMA sample
36 experience significant amplification ($\mu>1.1$)
We find that 20/29 *Herschel* DSFGs break down into multiple ALMA sources, implying a multiplicity rate of 69%.

results_numeric.quantity: Median S870 drop due to lensing

evidence.quote: the median flux density in the *Herschel*-ALMA sample drops by a factor of 1.6 when lensing is taken into account
with an intrinsic flux density of $S_{870} = 17.5 \pm 0.4\,$mJy

The median amplification in the subset that experiences lensing is $\mu_{870} =
            1.6$.

10$ compared to a random, uniformly distributed population

claims.hypothesis: Do bright Herschel DSFGs break into multiple ALMA sources at a high rate?
claims.experiment: Count ALMA components per Herschel source at 0.45 arcsec resolution
claims.finding: Brighter sources have higher multiplicity than ALESS

evidence.quote: Thus, the evidence favors brighter sources having a higher multiplicity rate.

claims.hypothesis: Are multiples closer together than random or simulated populations?
claims.experiment: dN/dA vs separation compared with random placement and two mock catalogs
claims.result: Excess ~10x at 0.5 arcsec; models under-predict small separations
claims.finding: Favors interactions/mergers, though blending not excluded

evidence.quote: This result suggests that a sophisticated treatment of blending yields better agreement between simulations and observations but the simulations still under-predict

claims.hypothesis: Which intrinsic number counts match measured magnifications?
claims.experiment: Compare P(mu>2) vs S870 for ALESS and COSMOS broken power-laws with data
claims.result: ALESS counts (steep fall off above 8 mJy) match better
claims.finding: Tentatively favors steep fall off above 8 mJy

evidence.quote: Number counts based on ALESS observations provide a better match to our magnification measurements.

why_this_method.value: Visibility-plane fitting avoids correlated pixel errors in cleaned images

evidence.quote: The best way to deal with this situation is to compare model and data visibilities rather than surface brightness maps.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Alternative HXMM30 model with sub-mm luminous lens deemed unlikely

evidence.quote: An alternative model in which the lens is sub-mm luminous cannot be ruled out, but we consider this unlikely for a number of reasons.

limitations_admitted.value: Resolution may cause over-predicted sizes and under-predicted magnifications; optically faint lenses may be missed

evidence.quote: in some cases the lens models may moderately over-predict the intrinsic sizes of the lensed galaxies and hence under-predict the magnification factors

referee_caveats_inferred: Many weakly lensed magnifications are maximal-lensing upper limits with fixed Einstein radii

Final MCMC phase of 10 iterations is short for uncertainty estimation
Number-count test relies on small sample and fixed lens/redshift model
